Resolves #20073

A tab dragged out of a popup's strip and dropped on main no longer leaves its header drag proxy floating over main: the drop retires the proxy generation its hover opened.

The ticket's window-pair hypothesis did not hold; the measured mechanism is now in its body. A pointer drag's `draggedItem` is the popup's tab header button, and the cross-window commit (`VesselWorkspace#commitCrossWindowTransfer`) settles only after the popup's own projection destroyed that button. `Base#destroy` deletes its own keys, so at the settle `Participation#getDragEmbodimentIdentity` read `itemId: undefined` and `VesselProxyEmbodiment#promote` resolved nothing. `Participation` now keeps the identity each frame staged under, and the frame's terminals resolve that one. `VesselProxyEmbodiment#reportUnresolved` logs an error when a promote or restore resolves nothing while a generation is still live in its own target window, which is the orphan the operator saw.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium Neural Link e2e on `apps/workstation` + unit) → L3 required (a cross-window pointer gesture). Residual: AC-4, Residual-Owner: #20022.

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: In Neo.mjs, `Base#destroy` deletes all own properties on the destroyed instance (`delete me[key]`). Any cross-window or asynchronous commit pipeline whose settlement handler identifies resources via properties on a dragged component (`draggedItem.dockItemId`) must snapshot that identity when the frame is staged (`Participation.#stagedIdentities`), because the commit's own projection can destroy the source component before the commit promise settles.
